follow100Note: Rows are rounded to cents, so the waterfall lands a cent above the $9.71 kept as profit on paper.
footerNote: Marvell guided Q3 FY26 revenue to $2.06B ±5%.
oneTimers: Marvell agreed in April 2025 to sell its automotive ethernet business to Infineon for $2.5B in cash; the sale closed August 14, 2025, after this quarter ended, so no gain appears here — the business sat as $595.5M of assets held for sale on the balance sheet, and the gain lands in Q3 FY26.

GAAP results include $153.6M of stock-based compensation and $243.7M of amortization of acquired intangible assets, both excluded from non-GAAP — that is why non-GAAP net income ($585.5M) is triple GAAP net income ($194.8M).
Restructuring related charges of $8.7M this quarter — severance and facility-exit costs, net.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $51.9M plus a $4.5M net other loss make up the $56.4M outside operations — no one-time gain sits here; the automotive ethernet sale closed after quarter end.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended August 2, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Data Center revenue hit $1.49B — 74% of the company — up 69% YoY on AI demand for custom silicon and electro-optics, and total revenue set a record at $2.01B, up 58% YoY.
takeaways.title: Data Center drove the record

takeaways.text: GAAP net income was $194.8M versus a $193.3M loss a year ago, as operating income swung to $290.1M from a $100.4M loss. Non-GAAP net income was $585.5M.
takeaways.title: Back in the black

takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $461.6M in the quarter, and Marvell spent $200M buying back its own shares and paid $51.7M in dividends.
takeaways.title: Cash kept flowing

verdict: Marvell's revenue hit a record $2.01B, up 58% on AI data-center demand — and GAAP profit swung to $195M from a $193M loss a year ago.
